question: A ladder makes an angle of 60° with the ground when placed against a wall. If the foot of the ladder is 2 m away from the wall, the length of the ladder is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle with angles 30°, 60°, and 90°, the side lengths are always in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The side adjacent to the 60° angle (base) corresponds to 1 ratio part.

The hypotenuse (the ladder) corresponds to the longest side, which is 2 ratio parts.

Given that the base distance is 2 m (1 part), the hypotenuse will be exactly double this length.

Length of the ladder = 2 × Base = 2 × 2 = 4 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall (Base) = 2 m

Angle made by the ladder with the ground (θ) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

cos(θ) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

 
 
 
 60° 
• 
• 2 m Wall Ladder (L) A B C 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of the ladder (Hypotenuse AC) be L.

⇒ In the right-angled ΔABC formed by the wall, ground, and ladder:

⇒ cos(60°) = BC ÷ AC

⇒ 1/2 = 2 ÷ L

⇒ L = 2 × 2

⇒ L = 4 m

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios (SOH CAH TOA)

In a right-angled triangle: sin(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, cos(θ) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Standard Trigonometric Values

Key values to remember for heights and distance: sin(30°) = 1/2, cos(30°) = √3/2. For 60° angles, sin(60°) = √3/2, cos(60°) = 1/2, and tan(60°) = √3.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation is formed when observing an object above the horizontal line of sight, while the angle of depression is formed when looking downwards from a height.
